name: Jianyu Long
headline:
Ideas into agents.
Research into things
that work.
intro: I’m Jianyu Long — I go by Westbrook. I study Data Science and Computer Science at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and build AI agents, voice interfaces, and machine learning systems.
about: My work connects model behavior with the systems around it: how agents remember, how speech becomes useful information, and how research implementations become runnable tools. I enjoy working across the stack, from data pipelines and model training to the interfaces people use.

projects.title: AI Pet
projects.subtitle: An agent with a memory
projects.description: A desktop companion with a tool-using agent loop and persistent personality. An evidence-governed memory pipeline combines structured updates, deterministic validation, and hybrid retrieval to keep context across sessions.
projects.detail: Layered memory · Tool permissions · Execution auditing

projects.title: Chastream
projects.subtitle: Conversations, made navigable
projects.description: An Android conversation intelligence platform that turns recordings into speaker-attributed transcripts, structured summaries, participant viewpoints, and timelines. Built across the mobile client, asynchronous audio pipeline, and cloud backend.

projects.title: Flow Voice
projects.subtitle: Your phone’s voice. Your desktop’s cursor.
projects.description: An open-source system that streams smartphone speech recognition directly into the active text cursor on Windows. Prefix matching and final-transcript reconciliation keep evolving speech results aligned without duplicate text.

projects.title: Training Planning Agent
projects.subtitle: Grounded plans, reviewed by agents
projects.description: Agent architecture for a deployed personalized training platform serving 20 users. Retrieval grounds plans in professional training guidelines and workout history; an evaluation-feedback loop checks constraints and consistency.

research.title: OneTrans
research.label: PyTorch reimplementation · Mar–Apr 2026
research.description: Ported a TensorFlow reference implementation into a modular training project, preserving heterogeneous feature tokenization and pyramid-style compression. Added schema-aware data loading, mixed precision, evaluation, and resumable checkpoints.

research.title: AI Mathematical Olympiad
research.label: Kaggle competition · 2024
research.description: Silver Medal, ranked 92nd of 2,212 teams (top 4.2%). Contributed an inference truncation strategy and data augmentation using bidirectional translation and LLM-generated mathematical samples.
research.tags: Mathematical reasoning / Language models / Data augmentation

experience.description: Built a road-roughness estimation pipeline from vehicle-mounted IMU data. Processed 7M+ multimodal data points and developed a Transformer–LSTM model deployed to the company’s cloud platform.
